turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mr Iyer, come, sit. What brings you in today?

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, umm, my grandson had a cricket match, I was going to tell you the whole score, but that is not it. I am having this cough in the morning, and the phlegm is brown.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Morning cough with brown phlegm. How long have you been having it?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Many years, doctor. Every morning I have to clear it. I left the cigarettes last year only, around Diwali.
[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He quit last November. Before that, nearly one packet a day, for something like twenty five years. I am the carer at the house, I used to hide the packets.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Haha, she did. My friends still smoke outside the tea stall and I just stand and gossip. The cough was already there in those days.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any blood mixed in the phlegm, or brown only?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): No blood. Brown, like weak tea, thicker in the morning, then it eases by itself.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest pain? Any tightness when you are walking?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No chest pain. My neighbour collapsed last month, big scene near the bakery, but I am not having any pain.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): And breathlessness? Has the weight come down?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): On the stairs to the terrace I get a little short of breath. Weight is stable. I still eat three idlis, though my wife is away at my daughter's place this month.
[SEG0013] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He has not lost weight. Same shirts. He finishes his meals.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any fever, or sweating in the night?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. Nights are ok, I sleep. It is only the morning cough business.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): What medicines are you taking these days? Tell me the doses if you remember.

[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Amlodipine 5 mg in the morning for the pressure. Atorvastation 20 mg at night for the cholesterol. Sugar tablets, metformin 500 mg twice a day for my sugar. And only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning, triphala, one small spoon, from the shop near the temple.
[SEG0018] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Also, he stopped the montelukast, montair 10 mg, in March. The chest doctor had written wysolone, that is prednisolone, but he never took it, not one tablet.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, I stopped montair in March, throat was feeling odd. Wysolone I never touched. Triphala I take daily, after my bath, before chai.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right, so the pressure, the sugar and the cholesterol are all on treatment. Did anyone do an x-ray or a breathing test before?

[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Two years back at the polyclinic they did a chest x-ray and they said it was borderline. I kept the film in the almirah and the monsoon finished it. The cricket bat is also in there, what to do.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me listen. Err, a few wheezes at both bases, no crackles. Your oxygen is 97 percent.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm. Is that serious?

[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am thinking this is chronic bronchitis, from the long smoking, the morning cough and the brown phlegm. COPD is still possible. I cannot separate the two without the lung numbers, so that part stays open.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Everyone says cancer, doctor. My cousin's father-in-law, long story, hospitals and all. Should I be frightened?

[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am not calling this cancer from what you have told me. The story fits the smoking and the bronchitis much better, and we will see what the tests show before we chase anything else.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): I will book the spirometry for Friday morning, nine o'clock, in the lung lab. You are not on an inhaler, so nothing to withhold that morning.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Friday at 9. Ok.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning, fasting sugar and lipids. Come fasting, no tea, skip the metformin that morning only, and take the amlodipine as usual.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): No chai on Thursday. That is the hard part, doctor. My chai is at six sharp.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Water is allowed, one morning only. If the spirometry comes back borderline, then we do a CT of the chest. I am not booking the scan now.
[SEG0032] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Doctor, the flu injection, should he take it? Last winter he was in bed a week and we never did any vaccine.

[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes. Kindly take the flu vaccine this month, and the pneumonia vaccine if you have not had it before. I am not giving the injection here today. The pharmacy downstairs can do the flu one.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): My brother took the pneumonia jab and his arm was paining for two days, he made more noise than my cough. Umm, I will ask at the pharmacy.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): A sore arm is ordinary, it is not your cough. I will see you in two weeks with the spirometry and the blood reports.
[SEG0036] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I will bring him Thursday and Friday, and again in two weeks. He misplaces the timings.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): If the shop is busy my nephew will open it. Small general store, nothing fancy. Thank you, doctor.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): Good. If you find any paper from that old x-ray, bring it, but do not worry if the film is gone.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. We will look in the almirah. Ok doctor.

spec.situation: Former smoker who quit last year with a long-standing morning cough and brown phlegm; weight stable; no chest pain; spirometry planned; vaccination advice.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

traps.happens: The patient lists medicines with their purpose ('amlodipine for the pressure', 'the cholesterol one at night', 'sugar tablets') and also mentions a herbal or shop remedy in passing ('only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning'). Their chronic conditions are never asked about directly.
traps.label_rule: Each medicine is recorded with the dose and timing said for THAT medicine; the herbal remedy is a medicine too (currently_used). A condition the patient states through its medicine ('for the pressure') is a past_medical_history entry ONLY if the patient actually said the condition name or its everyday name ('the pressure' = hypertension, normalized); do not invent a duration.

features: stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.

bad.reason: Drug and dose supported, but transcript says 'Atorvastation,' not explicitly atorvastatin.

omissions.text: Brown sputum described as 'like weak tea'.
Smoking cessation timing also stated by patient as around Diwali/last year.
Stopped montelukast (Montair) in March because the throat was 'feeling odd'.
Prednisolone/Wysolone had been prescribed by a chest doctor previously but the patient never took any tablets.
Past investigation detail: chest X-ray was done two years ago at the polyclinic and was reportedly described to him as 'borderline'.
Negative finding asked and answered: no chest tightness when walking.
Instruction that water is allowed while fasting before the blood tests.
Plan to bring any paperwork from the old chest X-ray if available.
